title: Amazon Customer Banned for Too Many Returns

image.attribution: Navy Petty Officer 1st Class Tim D. Godbee / Wikimedia Commons / Public Domain.

main_content:
Tuan Do of New York says Amazon has banned him from shopping on that website.

The reason? He returned too many Amazon purchases, he said on his website.

Do said he returned six items in the past two months.

Amazon first sent him a warning about his “unusually high rate of problems,” Do said.

Later, when his wife returned a bicycle purchased on her Amazon account, the company cancelled both their accounts, Do said.

Mark Cohen is former chairman of Sears Canada Inc. He is not surprised Amazon and other businesses are trying to stop returns.

The costs are very high for a company like Amazon that offers many customers both free delivery and free returns.

But banning a customer can create bad feelings.

Cohen, the former head of Sears Canada and now a Columbia University professor, said many returns are valid.

questions.question: Why was Tuan Do of New York banned from shopping on Amazon?
options: A) He failed to pay for his purchases.
B) He returned too many items.
C) He violated Amazon's terms of service.
questions.answer: B) He returned too many items.

questions.question: Why is Amazon trying to stop the returns?
options: A) It wants to maintain customer loyalty.
B) It is concerned about the high costs associated with returns.
C) It aims to improve its product selection.
D) It needs to increase its profit margins.
questions.answer: B) It is concerned about the high costs associated with returns.

questions.question: What can banning customers create?
options: C) Bad feelings among the customer base.
questions.answer: C) Bad feelings among the customer base.
